title: Sprints 6j to 6l: a project with its developer — Laptop, VM A and VM B

steps.say:
On the Laptop, 0-1. What this pass needs. The Laptop is the operator's own computer and the host admin: rent, prepare, its installation VPN, admit walkadmin, register, take off, lock, purge and give back. Every host, Core and Matrix check and both gathered-push invocations run here in the Claude Code session launched from the credential-preparation terminal in step 1-2, as ! bash …. That session inherits the dedicated Git helper; no global helper setting is changed. The Laptop also creates the private GitHub repositories; VM A seeds them as walkadmin.

VM A is the Ubuntu 26.04 libvirt VM walk-laptop-c at 192.168.122.245. Its existing desktop account is walkadmin (uid 1000, sudo), the project admin, whose host laptop name is walklaptop at 10.73.<n>.3. VM B is test-ubuntu-vm, 192.168.122.174, with its console and the developer account walkdev. The operator starts with both VM accounts ready. VM A and VM B both run laptop-b-*.sh; the Laptop runs laptop-a-repositories.sh, and VM A runs laptop-a-seed.sh. Those file names stay as written. Keep both VMs isolated from concurrent VPN/internal-host changes until cleanup.

Agent Machines, the VMs' admin, owns setup and teardown from the Laptop. Start only after its preparation is confirmed: it has copied the handover to /var/tmp/walk23 on both VMs, checked SHA256SUMS against SHA256SUMS.sha256 and every listed file, installed dpkg-repack on both, and run `sudo PORELO_WALK_DEVELOPER=walkadmin bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-make.sh <walk23-digest>` on VM A and `sudo bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-make.sh <walk23-digest>` on VM B. It preserves VM A's existing walkadmin password and sudo, and creates walkdev with a password it sets and leaves on the Laptop in ~/.porelo/keys/test-ubuntu-vm-walkdev.password (0600); walkadmin's password is in ~/.porelo/keys/walk-laptop-c-walkadmin.password (0600). After the operator's last step, Agent Machines runs `sudo bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-remove.sh` on VM B from its admin login and on VM A, restores the recorded package/account state, removes the pass's trusted host CAs and restores Firefox's prior policy, removes /var/tmp/walk23 on both, and checks that no porelo VPN link is left. The removal script reads each VM's recorded account; walkadmin's preexisting account is kept. Setup, teardown and their checks belong to the agent, not to the operator.

Host: walk6. Project: walk6-demo. Allow about 90 minutes (a guess), including the host guide's approximately 20 minutes of checks and Core/Matrix's approximately 5 minutes each. One server with its forge is rented and given back. This pass still uses the per-person VPNs while normal work moves to ssh alone.

On the Laptop have the Scaleway key/project UUID, rental SSH pair, sudo password, ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx and master password; GitHub credentials for the private repositories porelo-ai/walk6-demo and porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access. The operator's token has Contents write and Administration on exactly those two. Record its existing GitHub token name as <walk23-token-name> for explicit revocation at cleanup; never record the token value in the panel. VM A uses the same operator GitHub account and token rights, entered separately in Git's in-memory helper and Your forges; its signing key is its own, generated on VM A before seed, and seeds there with that protected key in its agent. project.yml lists walkadmin's public line alone; this same line is carried to the Laptop for registration and to VM B for verification. No operator signing key is needed. VM B uses the developer's actual GitHub test-account login/token and accepts both read invitations. Each machine's local Porelo-Vault must also reach these private URLs: have its existing vault passphrase, or choose a new one when the conditional vault init in its follow step asks. Newly added local git.token.github.com entries are removed in cleanup; existing credentials are preserved.

The Laptop needs Flutter/Dart from pubspec.yaml, Linux desktop build tools, a working local Porelo and unlocked secret store, Bash, git, ssh, scp, ssh-keygen, curl, jq, python3, python3-yaml, sha256sum, wg, wg-quick, keepassxc-cli, sudo, ip, ping, openssl and update-ca-certificates. Both VMs need a desktop secret store, wl-clipboard (wl-copy) on a Wayland desktop or xclip on X11 for keepassxc-cli clip, Bash, git, python3, ssh, scp, ssh-keygen, wg, wg-quick, keepassxc-cli, sudo, update-ca-certificates and the Linux system tools checked by join: sh, ip, ping, cat, install, date, sleep, awk, cmp, mktemp, chmod, mv, rm, grep, head, tail, sed, base64, id, stat and mkdir. The agents' preparation includes dpkg-repack on both VMs; start needs tar and pgrep. Porelo comes from the handover. Ansible runs on the host.

Keep porelo-host doc/guides/6-host.md at 107f786 and its 13 scripts in ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/ beside you, including 6-host-push-run.sh. Core: ~/.porelo/handover/porelo/6-pass/porelo-checks.md; Matrix: ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-message-matrix/6-pass/6-matrix.md. Verify intended host snapshots before starting: Core 3c5b5eff or later and Matrix 982e063 or later; keep them stable. The collection is ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282/porelo-host-0.5.9-snapshot.tar.gz, SHA-256 005fcd24363aebcac123e6d50df5dc8510461d7a2576ea240baac3d0ac32913e.

The shared handover is ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23/ on the Laptop and /var/tmp/walk23 on both VMs. It holds the debug bundle, shared VM scripts, laptop-a-seed.sh, porelo_0.5.1~snapshot.900+local.20261029T192331_amd64.deb, SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sha256. For the operator's laptop-b-start.sh invocations only, read the manifest digest in a separate terminal on the Laptop (not run):

cat ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23/SHA256SUMS.sha256

Keep this value as <walk23-digest>; never substitute a different manifest's digest. The interface bundle must include the join fix 2a79f67, which removes prior secrets-file selection; use this main checkout's interface sources. The bundle must include the published bring wizard from 93651c9 and the hand-over/start/make/remove scripts from 9794174. VM A creates its encrypted secrets file before bring in step 5-4; the wizard chooses that existing file.

Expected: (not run) all three machines and artifacts are identified, VM A owns its signing private key, and its sole public signer is used for seed, host registration, bring and Developers. Failure signs: agent preparation unconfirmed, either account unavailable, missing tool/snapshot, wrong start digest, an older join bundle or an older bring bundle. The project pins walkadmin alone. The PR uses walkdev’s intermediate change followed by a signed empty walkadmin commit; Forgejo fast-forwards that exact signed tip after walkadmin’s approval. Main must not move during the PR and the approver must differ from its author. The Laptop, VM A and VM B all follow https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git; the host accounts keep their file-bundle follows. No live step is rehearsed. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 0-2. VM A's existing walkadmin password is held only in ~/.porelo/keys/walk-laptop-c-walkadmin.password, mode 0600. Read it privately on the Laptop outside Claude Code, terminal recording, logs and this panel; never paste it here or print it into an agent session. Use it at VM A's console login and sudo prompts. Its SSH account accepts keys only; this password is for the ready desktop account, not for handover transfer. Expected: (not run) walkadmin's existing password is available privately and its existing sudo membership is kept. Failure signs: missing/unreadable password file, broader permissions or password exposed in a transcript. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 0-3. Start the interface from ~/git/porelo-frontend in a separate terminal that stays open (not run):

bash tool/start_host_walk.sh --visible --roles host-admin 23 ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282

Expected: (not run) the collection matches its manifest, the Linux debug bundle opens with the host-admin role and this panel is visible. Failure signs: start-host-walk: step 0-1 failed, missing role commands or a build failure. Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-4. Log into the console as walkadmin. Before VM A runs seed, generate walkadmin's own signing key in a separate terminal. Use a passphrase-protected key and a dedicated SSH agent: the private file stays encrypted on VM A, and Git's requested .pub configuration uses the loaded key without repeated GUI prompts. Never copy the private key. Run each command in order (not run); stop for existing keys and never approve an overwrite:

mkdir -p ~/.ssh

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

test ! -e ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

test ! -e ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C '' -f ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

Choose and repeat a new test-only key passphrase at ssh-keygen's prompts. Rewrite its public file without a comment or trailing space (not run), typing that passphrase when asked:

ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/walk6-signing > ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub
 Start the account's dedicated test agent and load that key (not run):

eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"

ssh-add ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

At ssh-add's prompt type the same key passphrase. Configure Git (not run):

git config --global gpg.format ssh

git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

git config --global commit.gpgsign true

git config --global user.name 'Walk project admin'

git config --global user.email walkadmin@example.org

Print only its comment-free public line (not run):

awk '{print $1, $2}' ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

Carry that public line only to the Laptop for registration at step 5-2 and to VM B for follow/join. VM A's seed reads this same file from Git's user.signingkey; it accepts one comment-free ssh-ed25519 line alone. Keep this terminal open for the next step: the interface must inherit its SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Expected: (not run) ssh-add confirms the key was loaded, Git selects the public file and the private half remains only on VM A. Failure signs: no agent, key not loaded, wrong passphrase, wrong key type or private data copied. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-5. In the same walkadmin terminal used for the signing-agent setup in step 0-4, enable the account’s daemon (not run):

systemctl --user enable --now porelod

Check it (not run):

systemctl --user is-active porelod

Then start the desktop interface from this same terminal, so it inherits the loaded signing agent, using the shared handover (not run):

PORELO_WALK_DEVELOPER=walkadmin PORELO_WALK_ROLES=project-admin bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-start.sh <walk23-digest>

Expected: (not run) active is printed and VM A's interface starts with project-admin, with no host-admin actions. Failure signs: failed unit, checksum refusal, no desktop or role error. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-6. In the title bar click Copy my public keys for a host…. In Copy my public keys for a host, type walk6 into Host name, then Copy my public keys. Check Public keys for walk6 copied., then Close. Carry this YAML's public ssh_public_key and wireguard_public_key to the Laptop: type the two public lines there, or save them with a text editor on VM A as /tmp/walkadmin-public.yml, then make that public-only file readable (not run):

chmod 644 /tmp/walkadmin-public.yml

Type the public text on the Laptop, or fetch this public-only file from the Laptop with ~/.ssh/porelo-vm-admin, whose public key Agent Machines installed in walkadmin's authorized_keys (not run):

scp -i ~/.ssh/porelo-vm-admin -o IdentitiesOnly=yes walkadmin@192.168.122.245:/tmp/walkadmin-public.yml /tmp/walkadmin-public.yml Expected: (not run) VM A's per-host private halves stay in walkadmin's secret store, while the Laptop receives only the two public fields. Failure signs: wrong host, extra/private fields, secret-store refusal or changed public text. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-1. In a separate terminal in your own login, from ~/git/porelo-frontend, run (not run):

bash tool/walk23/laptop-a-repositories.sh

At Developer GitHub login, type the developer test account's actual GitHub login. Alternatively set PORELO_GUIDE_DEVELOPER_LOGIN before running; an explicitly empty value skips the optional invitation, which this pass needs. At the hidden GitHub token prompt, type the operator's token for exactly porelo-ai/walk6-demo and porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access and Enter. It needs repository Administration for creation/invitations; the Laptop’s Git credentials need Contents write for gathered pushes; VM A’s separate Git credentials seed the repositories in step 1-4. Expected: (not run) both repository states, the developer account and any existing project permission are checked before the first mutation; both repositories are private and the developer is granted/invited read access (permission pull) to walk6-demo only; laptop-a-repositories passed. The access repository's developer invitation belongs to Developers later. Failure signs: a public repository, invalid login, a login with existing stronger access, or an API refusal. Return to this panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-2. Use a new separate terminal in your own account for the walk's Git environment and check session. The API script's token prompt does not fill Git's helper. Do not change global git config. Set a private, walk-only in-memory credential cache and environment overrides (not run):

mkdir -p ~/.porelo/walk23-git

chmod 700 ~/.porelo/walk23-git

export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.helper

export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="cache --timeout=3600 --socket=$HOME/.porelo/walk23-git/credential.sock"

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=credential.useHttpPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=false

The empty helper resets inherited helpers only in these processes, the next selects this cache, and credential.useHttpPath=false lets the host-push runner's github.com-only lookup reuse it. Read the private repository with this command's own helper (not run):

git -c credential.helper= -c "credential.helper=$GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1" ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git HEAD

At Username type the operator's actual GitHub login; at Password type the restricted token. The empty pre-seed repository may print no hash; require no authentication error. Start the Claude Code session used for all ! bash guide checks from this same terminal in ~/git/porelo-frontend (not run):

claude

Those check scripts inherit GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE, including both gathered-push runners, without any script edit or global helper write. If the one-hour cache expires, repeat the credential read in a terminal with these same exports before its next use. Expected: (not run) the dedicated helper supplies this pass's publishing credential; the operator's existing helper/config file is unchanged. Failure signs: checks launched from a session missing these exports, expired credentials, authentication refusal or a token in a file/log/argument. Return to the panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 1-3. walkadmin uses the operator's GitHub account and restricted token (Contents write and Administration on exactly the two private walk repositories). Close VM A's interface and return to its original signing/start terminal from step 0-4, preserving the signing agent. Set this terminal's private helper environment (not run):

mkdir -p ~/.porelo/walk23-git

chmod 700 ~/.porelo/walk23-git

export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.helper

export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="cache --timeout=3600 --socket=$HOME/.porelo/walk23-git/credential.sock"

export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=credential.useHttpPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=false

Read both remotes with each command's own helper (not run):

git -c credential.helper= -c "credential.helper=$GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1" ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git HEAD

git -c credential.helper= -c "credential.helper=$GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1" ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access.git HEAD

At Username type the operator's actual login; at Password type the restricted token. The second read reuses the in-memory cache. Seed in step 1-4 and the restarted interface inherit these overrides; their Git subprocesses use them without a global credential.helper write. An empty remote may print no HEAD hash; require successful authentication. The signing key remains ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub, with its protected private half loaded in this terminal's agent. Prepare the encrypted file in step 5-4 before bring. Expected: (not run) both remotes are readable and no existing global helper is changed. Failure signs: wrong account/token, expired one-hour cache, missing exports/agent or authentication refusal. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 1-4. After laptop-a-repositories.sh on the Laptop and VM A's Git credentials in step 1-3, use the original signing/start terminal where step 1-3 closed the interface and exported its helper environment, which still has the dedicated SSH_AUTH_SOCK and loaded signing key. Run as walkadmin (not run):

bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-a-seed.sh

The script reads git's user.signingkey, requires exactly one comment-free ssh-ed25519 public line, and lists that line alone in project.yml. The protected private key in walkadmin's agent signs both initial commits. Git's in-memory helper supplies the operator's GitHub token; no private signing key is copied. project.yml names guarded, its image/repository, the private access repository and a Matrix peer; access.yml starts with developers: {}, with host and Matrix settings written by bring. Both remotes are checked before either is published. An identical signed seed is kept; different content is refused. Expected: (not run) both signed main hashes are read back and laptop-a-seed passed, with walkadmin's sole public signer. Failure signs: missing/malformed/commented user.signingkey, absent agent/key, signing or credential refusal, different content or push refusal. Restart VM A's interface from this same terminal with step 0-5's start command after seed passes. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-5. In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-host.md, laptop-prepare:

! bash ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/6-host-laptop-prepare.sh

Expected: (not run) tools, host and Matrix manifests, GitHub read access and the collection pass; laptop-prepare passed is printed. Failure signs: a missing tool, checksum mismatch or GitHub read refusal; creation and seeding have already completed. Record a finding by its step name; return to this panel afterward. Next in the panel moves on, including when the check was already done.

On the Laptop, 1-6. Before using Follow it, prepare this LOCAL Porelo account's vault connection in a separate terminal; Git's cache and Your forges do not populate it. Read status (not run):

porelo vault status

Exit 0 means open, 3 shut, 4 absent. Only for exit 4, create a vault (not run):

porelo vault init

Type a new test-only Porelo-Vault passphrase twice at New vault passphrase: and New vault passphrase again:. For exit 3, unlock it (not run):

porelo vault unlock

Enter its existing passphrase; never clear or replace an existing vault. This is the account's Porelo-Vault, separate from the KeePassXC secrets file. Once open, list names only (not run):

porelo vault list

Inspect declared connections as well; names and locations only are shown (not run):

porelo credentials list

Preserve any existing matching GitHub connection and either fallback entry git.token.github.com or git.token. Do not shadow an existing generic git.token with a new host-specific entry. Only if there is no matching connection and neither git.token.github.com nor git.token exists, store the operator’s restricted GitHub token from step 1-1 at its hidden Value for 'git.token.github.com': prompt (not run):

porelo vault put git.token.github.com

Record that this pass added the entry for later removal. If a matching connection or fallback already exists, preserve it and record that it must not be removed in cleanup; stop for the account's credential owner if it does not reach these repositories. Check this exact destination without printing a value (not run):

porelo credentials check https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git --no-connect

Require ready before returning to the interface. Decline any offer to replace/remove a preexisting credential, and stop for its owner if this destination is not ready. Any Porelo-Vault passphrase/token is typed only in this separate terminal, never in a command line or the panel. In the rail click Projects, then Follow a project by its address. Type walk6-demo in What the project is called — the name in its project.yml, and exactly https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git in Where the project's own repository is. In How its commits are checked choose Only commits signed with this key; paste only walkadmin's comment-free public signing line carried from VM A in step 0-4 into The public key, or its fingerprint. Click Follow it, then Go to it after verification. Expected: (not run) this Laptop account follows that exact GitHub URL, pinned to walkadmin alone, and the seed commit is applied. Failure signs: a forge/file URL used instead, missing local Porelo, credential/signature refusal or an unverified follow. Messages are not set up before bring writes the host/Matrix access settings. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 2-1. In the interface: click Prepare a server… in the title bar, the server icon right of Watch another machine…. Expected: (not run) the wizard Prepare a server opens at Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented, showing Scaleway project id and Set Scaleway key, with no Account on the server field. Failure signs: no server icon in the title bar (--roles host-admin was omitted at startup), or its tooltip reads Prepare a server… with a reason after it (keepassxc-cli is missing).

On the Laptop, 2-2. In the interface (Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented): type your Scaleway project UUID into Scaleway project id (if your Scaleway key is not stored yet, click Set Scaleway key first and enter it in its terminal), then click Next. Expected: (not run) the Scaleway key check succeeds and Step 2 of 7 — Your server opens, proposing the lowest unused network number <n> (such as 0) with Run a forge on this server turned on; no project step is shown. Failure signs: Copy the project id from Scaleway Project, Settings. below Next, or a Scaleway key error keeping the wizard on Step 1.

On the Laptop, 2-3. In the interface (Step 2 of 7 — Your server): type walk6 into Server name, keep the proposed integer <n> in Network number (0–255) (note <n> for the 10.73.<n>.0/24 and porelo-<n> checks below), leave Run a forge on this server turned on, and click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys opens. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with This laptop already knows a host with that name or network. Choose another. or The server name needs one DNS label….

In the interface (Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys): enter your rental SSH private key path (such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) in Your private ssh key, confirm Your public ssh key holds the matching .pub path with a check mark, and click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file opens with ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx in Your secrets file (.kdbx), It is there: setup opens it with its master password., and Open it now. Failure signs: a refusal on Your public ssh key saying the pair does not match, or a missing key file keeping Next disabled.

On the Laptop, 2-5. In the interface (Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file): confirm ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx is in Your secrets file (.kdbx), click Open it now, type the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx into the terminal and press Enter, then click Done. Expected: (not run) nothing you type is shown; keepassxc-cli records hosts/walk6/wireguard in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx and the terminal prints The secrets file is ready.; after Done, the step shows Ready: the file keeps the server’s keys. On the Laptop, 2-6. In the interface (Step 4 to Step 5 of 7 — the Laptop test collection, shown in a development build): click Next, type /home/<you>/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282/porelo-host-0.5.9-snapshot.tar.gz (your home in place of /home/<you>) into Test collection (.tar.gz) and 005fcd24363aebcac123e6d50df5dc8510461d7a2576ea240baac3d0ac32913e into Test collection SHA-256, then click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 6 of 7 — Check and start opens with the summary Scaleway project id: …, Server: walk6, Network: 10.73.<n>.0/24, Forge: on, No project or project account is created., your SSH keys, Secrets file: ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx, and the test collection, plus the button Prepare the server. Failure signs: Give the test collection SHA-256 as 64 hexadecimal digits. or The test collection does not exist….

On the Laptop, 2-7. In the interface (Step 6 of 7 — Check and start): verify every line of the summary, then click Prepare the server — from here on a server is rented — and when Step 7 of 7 — Preparing the server pauses at its stop, click Complete setup on the host. Expected: (not run) porelo-host up runs with --host-name walk6 --network <n> --login-user root --forge true and no project bundle or project account, then pauses waiting for you; Complete setup on walk6 opens asking only for the host's VPN key and its forge's certificate from your secrets file (no vault passphrase, no vault entries, no Tresorit login, no Matrix token). Failure signs: a refused step in the protocol, or Complete setup on walk6 asking for any secret other than wireguard and forge-certificate.

On the Laptop, 2-8. In the interface (Complete setup on walk6): click Open the terminal, type only the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx once into the terminal and press Enter (nothing else is asked), then click Done. Expected: (not run) nothing you type is shown; a lasting CA for walk6 is stored in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx under hosts/walk6/forge-ca-key and hosts/walk6/forge-ca (constrained to walk6.porelo.internal and 10.73.<n>.0/24), certificates for forge.walk6.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6.porelo.internal are signed locally, wireguard and forge-certificate are piped to porelo-host-stop --stdin, and the terminal says The host has what it needs; setup goes on.; Done closes the stop dialog and resumes up. Failure signs: has no entry hosts/walk6/wireguard; nothing was sent., The host's certificates could not be signed; nothing was sent., or Host setup ended with code 64: a wrong call.

On the Laptop, 2-9. In the interface: wait for up to end ready (up checked in the protocol, and For the project admins shown below it). When Bring the VPN up for walk6 opens by itself, click Cancel it twice and click Finish so step 3-1 brings the VPN up from walk6's row in Machines (if you already typed your sudo password there, click Finish and go on). Then click Next in this panel. Expected: (not run) up ends ready with host.json checked. Failure signs: host.json is missing from the completed server setup. or a host.json mismatch in the protocol.

On the Laptop, 3-1. In the interface: in the rail click Machines. On walk6's row, which says In preparation, click Open the host protocol and in it click Bring the VPN up — or, if walk6 already shows as Prepared, click its chevron (Show more), open its menu (⋮), run Take the VPN down with your sudo password, then open its menu (⋮) again and click Bring the VPN up to exercise the machine row's VPN command. Type only your sudo password into Bring the VPN up for walk6 and press Enter, verify the tunnel on the Laptop, then come back here. Expected: (not run) the terminal installs porelo-<n>, confirms a fresh WireGuard handshake, trusts walk6's CA and writes forge.walk6.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6.porelo.internal into /etc/hosts; walk6 stands in Machines as Prepared. In a separate terminal on the Laptop, ip -br addr show porelo-<n> shows 10.73.<n>.2/32 and ping -c 1 10.73.<n>.1 answers (not run). Failure signs: The VPN check did not confirm this server., snap confinement, a network collision, walk6 staying in preparation or no reply. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 3-2. In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-host.md, host-prepare:

! bash ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/6-host-prepare.sh

Expected: (not run) host.json matches, no people or projects exist, forge and homeserver answer 200, helpers and the sync sudo rule exist; host-prepare passed. Failure signs: any expected: / got: mismatch, a nonzero exit, or the named passed line missing. Record a finding by its step name; return to this panel afterward. Next in the panel moves on, including when the check was already done.
